ABOUT DOCKER

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.

We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.

_______________________________________________________________________




THE ROLE

Docker Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) embed directly with our most strategic customers to solve important, complex technical problems and turn ambitious ideas into production outcomes. FDEs take on the most challenging technical challenges using existing Docker products and patterns when possible, and work across customer, Docker Product and Engineering teams to realize new approaches when required.

 

As a Docker FDE, you will work side-by-side with customer engineering teams to deeply understand their goals, problems, constraints, and technical landscape; identify the highest-leverage opportunities; and design, build, and ship solutions with them. You own the technical journey from discovery and architecture through prototyping, implementation and production rollout.

 

The solutions you build may use existing Docker products, extend Docker into new environments, integrate deeply with customer and third-party systems, or reveal capabilities that Docker should build next. You work closely with Docker Solutions Architects to evolve existing patterns, and Docker Product and Engineering to turn new learnings into reusable patterns and product capabilities.

_______________________________________________________________________

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

Build in Production with Customers

 - Embed with customer engineering teams to design, build, and ship solutions from first prototype through stable production rollout. Use existing Docker products and patterns when possible, invent, prototype and validate innovative solutions when necessary.

 - Deliver working technical artifacts to customers: custom MCP servers with tightly integrated Docker Sandbox environments for coding agents and containerized agents; Docker Compose definitions for multi-agent harnesses and model-backed applications; Hardened Image standardization and migration; New tools that unblock customer progress.

 - Integrate Docker's AI platform with the customer's existing stack, including identity providers (OIDC/SAML/SSO), secrets management, private and air-gapped registries, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, and observability tooling.

 - Own technical delivery on your engagements: scope the work, sequence it, make trade-offs between speed and quality, remove blockers early, and contribute directly to code whenever progress depends on it.

Make AI Adoption Safe and Governable

 - Translate customer security, compliance, and platform requirements into concrete plans and see those plans through from ideation to production.

 - Help customers define controls to enable them to adopt agentic AI to solve their unique business problems without compromising security, compliance, data sovereignty or end-user experience.

 - Establish quality and performance standards for customers and work closely with Docker Product and Engineering to quickly address issues that fall outside of established thresholds

 - Partner with customer security and platform teams to get agentic workloads through architecture review, threat modeling, and change control.

Partner with Solutions Architecture and the Field

 - Work closely with Solutions Architects to enable off-the-self solutions when possible and provide technical experience and leadership when a bespoke solution is necessary.

 - Feed implementation learnings back into reference architectures, SOW templates, and success patterns so that FDE innovations become standard features and implementation patterns.

 - Support the field with technical depth during proofs of concept, escalations, and expansion conversations when a working build is the fastest path to a customer adoption.

Close the Loop with Product and Engineering

 - As part of Docker Engineering FDEs work closely with Product and Engineering teams to fold FDE innovations, learnings, and design patterns into existing or new products and services.

 - Work with Customers, Product and Engineering to establish quality and performance thresholds, ensuring customer environments meet them consistently, and responding quickly and decisively when they don’t.

 - Be the voice of the customer. Deliver data-driven and actionable feedback to Product and Engineering: what works well; what does not; what customers are asking for; and what blocks their adoption and forward progress. FDE experience directly influences the roadmap.

Shape the Practice

 - Define the FDE engagement model, delivery standards, and quality bar, and codify them so that engagements are consistent across customers, regions, and delivery partners.

 - Mentor and lead other Forward Deployed Engineers, and participate in hiring loops to grow the team.

 - Act as the senior technical escalation point on the hardest problems impacting your customers. Every incident is an opportunity to improve Docker products and services.

 - Maintain deep, current knowledge of the agentic AI stack: LLMs, APIs, MCP, coding agents, model and harness evaluation approaches, performance and quality thresholds, deployment patterns.

 - This role may require participation in an on-call rotation to provide support outside of standard business hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, as needed.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Architect, deploy, and operate AWS infrastructure across compute, messaging, storage, networking, and observability.

Competitive salary and employee stock options. Visa sponsorship is not available.

Remote within Europe, with residence within three hours of Central European Time.

description:
About Notabene

Notabene is on a mission to make crypto a part of the everyday economy. Leading crypto organizations use our tools to reduce transaction risk and make crypto transfers safe. Working across three continents in eight countries, the Notabene team serves our fantastic community of 100+ customers, including financial institutions, fintechs, exchanges, and more. Our co-founders spearheaded foundational Self Sovereign Identity protocols and use-cases. This technology is key to the internals of our cutting edge tech stack.

We’re proud to have the support of leading investors, including Y Combinator, Jump Capital, Castle Island, Green Visor Capital, and more.

We’re at an exhilarating moment in our journey, as regulation technologies (reg-techs) are fast becoming recognized as a vital enabler of the crypto ecosystem. Notabene is growing fast—and we’re looking for people like you to help shape the future rails of the crypto industry!



The Impact You'll Have:

Every crypto transfer we touch moves between institutions that run their own systems, answer to different regulators, and have no reason to trust each other. The software in the middle has to be right every time. A message processed twice, a lost update, or a record shown to the wrong tenant is a compliance failure for our customers.

You’ll work on the core platform that carries this data between institutions around the world, written in Go.

As a Staff Engineer on the team you’ll build the hardest parts of it, contribute to its design, and help the engineers around you do their best work.



What You'll Do

 - Design and build core parts of our transaction platform.

 - Build for correctness under failure, with the isolation and auditability a regulated product needs.

 - Scale the platform as transaction volume and the number of institutions per node grow, keeping latency predictable and the database healthy.

 - Write design docs for what you build, and give sharp, useful reviews on other people’s designs and code.

 - Build with AI agents every day, and help improve the specs, context and review practices that make agent-written code safe to ship in a regulated product.

 - Work with product, compliance and customer-facing teams to turn regulatory and customer needs into working software.

 - Own what you ship in production, from tracing and alerts to incident follow-ups.

 - Mentor engineers on the team.

 - Work on an on call rotation



Must Haves

 - Systems design depth. You’ve designed and owned distributed systems where correctness matters more than features. You know asynchronous processing well and can reason about what happens when parts of it fail.

 - Strong Go, or deep production experience in another statically typed backend language (Java, Kotlin, Rust, C#) and the appetite to be shipping Go within your first weeks.

 - PostgreSQL in depth: schema design, query plans, locking and isolation levels, migrations on live systems, and multi-tenant data.

 - End-to-end ownership in the cloud. Working knowledge of AWS or GCP: IAM, networking, managed databases, queues and storage. You can read and change Terraform and debug production from traces and logs.

 - AI-native engineering. You use coding agents such as Claude Code or Cursor every day and can show how. You write the specs and context, break work down for them, and review their output as hard as a human pull request. You know where they fail.

 - Staff-level experience. A track record of delivering large, technically hard projects end to end and helping the engineers around you get better. Typically 8+ years building backend systems.

 - Clear, concise writing in a remote company that makes decisions in documents and async threads.

 - Security fundamentals for sensitive data: encryption in transit and at rest, key handling, minimising personal data, and least-privilege access.



Nice-to-Haves

 - Applied cryptography: encryption, signing and key management.

 - Decentralized identity: DIDs, verifiable credentials, DIDComm.

 - Regulated finance, payments or compliance: Travel Rule, AML, ISO 20022.

 - Building and running software under SOC 2 or ISO 27001 controls.

 - Crypto and blockchain knowledge: chains, addresses, assets, CAIP identifiers.

 - Node.js and TypeScript.

 - Queue and workflow systems, and modern observability tooling.



Benefits

 - Flexible Remote Work: Work from anywhere!

 - $1000 WFH Stipend: Use within your first year of employment.

 - MacBook Pro: Procured by you and your manager to find a model that meets your needs.

 - Unlimited PTO: We trust you to take as much holiday as you need.

 - Country-Specific Benefits: Statutory offerings and contributions, managed via our employer-of-record.



Apply Today!

If you strongly believe this role is for you, please apply. Notabene considers a broad array of candidates, including those without blockchain experience. Whether you’re returning to work after a gap in employment, or taking the next step in your career path, we will be glad to have you on our radar.

Notabene is proud to be an equal employment workplace and an affirmative action employer. By valuing inclusion and diversity of all forms, we strictly prohibit and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, ancestry, citizenship, sexual orientation, status as a protected veteran, or any other legally protected characteristic.

description:
ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for Engineering Managers to lead engineering effort on Supabase Spark. Supabase Spark is an initiative to build the next frontier of agentic databases, supporting billions of databases, with millions of databases created every day.

Although we don’t require managers to contribute to code directly, we do expect you to participate in design discussions and to be involved in setting the bar for engineering quality and best practices.




WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR



Team & People

 - Build a healthy, high-trust team culture in a remote-first, globally distributed environment.

 - Run 1:1s, performance management, career development, and onboarding for your direct reports.

 - Handle people admin (leave, time off, etc.) for your team.

Hiring

 - Own the hiring plan for your team and act as Hiring Manager. First round of interviewer for all roles on the team.

 - Partner with Talent Acquisition to source, interview, and close strong candidates.

 - Contribute to headcount planning, org design, and the evolution of engineering leadership at Supabase.

Delivery & Roadmap

 - Own the team's roadmap and project management (Linear), driving accountability and clear milestones.

 - Manage workflow intake and Slack triage. These are the team’s primary inboxes for cross-team requests. You decide what gets routed where, prioritized, or pushed back on.

 - Own the team's weekly updates and keep stakeholders aligned without creating overhead.

 - Organize effort against support tickets and maintain the team's SLO.

 - Surface risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs early and clearly to leadership.

Incident Commander

 - Train as an Incident Commander. Drive coordination, resolution, and post-incident follow-up.

 - Lead blameless post-incident reviews
   


YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

 - Have 5+ years of engineering background, with enough depth to be credible with engineers building complex systems.

 - Have 3+ years managing remote engineering teams.

 - Have managed engineering teams at a cloud, SaaS, or developer tools company.

 - Experience with developer tools or databases, plus if that includes both SQLite and Postgres ecosystems.

 - Strong technical credibility in backend and database systems: APIs, auth, and Postgres access control (roles, grants, RLS) etc.

 - Has led a team shipping a developer facing API or platform product from early stage to production.

 - Have managed remote, globally distributed teams that work asynchronously across disparate time zones.

 - Are technical enough to be credible with strong engineers, but genuinely passionate about people management. This is the work you want to do, not a track you're settling for.

 - Build psychological safety and a feedback culture: you give feedback often and in the moment, ask for it back, and create space for the team to do the same.

 - Operate as a multiplier. Focused on helping individuals achieve more than they could alone, not on being the best technical voice in the room.

 - Coach rather than direct. Remove blockers, connect people to context and resources, and trust your engineers to own how the work gets done.

 - Have a real track record of performance management and can speak to specific examples of difficult conversations and how you navigated them.

 - Are comfortable with ambiguity and capable of building structure where there isn't much.

 - Communicate clearly and write well. You're default async, default written, set context proactively, and surface risks early.

 - Are collaborative, low-ego, and adaptable. You thrive working with high-autonomy, senior ICs who have strong technical opinions and don't need to be the smartest person in the room.

 - Are comfortable with aggressive scoping and eval driven development.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Fully Remote
   
   We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

 - ESOP
   
   Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

 - Tech Allowance
   
   Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

 - Health Benefits
   
   Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

 - Annual Off-Sites
   
   Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

 - Flexible Work
   
   We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

 - Professional Development
   
   Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.
   
   


ABOUT THE TEAM

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

 - ~400 team members

 - 60+ countries

 - 20+ languages spoken

 - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

 - 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: Data Engineering Lead
description:
ABOUT PLASMA

Plasma is building the primary account for global money.

Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders.  Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.

Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.

Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.

The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.






THE TEAM & OUR STORY https://x.com/Plasma/status/2067634709727719601?s=20

We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.

We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.



The Role

We're looking for a hands-on Data Lead to build Plasma's data function from the ground up. You'll be our first dedicated data hire, working across Consumer, Payments and Business to give the company one trusted view of its users, its money and its operations.

At first you'll build much of the platform yourself: our Snowflake warehouse, the pipelines that feed it and the modelled layer on top. As the function grows, you'll choose the tools, set the standards and hire the team.

The Work

 - Own Plasma's data platform end to end: the Snowflake warehouse, ingestion from production systems and third-party providers, and the modelled layer the rest of the company builds on

 - Define the metrics the company runs on, including funded users, activation, engagement, balances, spend and retention, and make sure every team uses the same definitions

 - Partner with Consumer to understand how users behave across regions, segments and products, and turn that into specific product decisions

 - Design and analyse experiments, and be clear about when a result is real and when it isn't

 - Work with Payments and finance so the business can trust its numbers: reconciliation across ledgers, providers and banking partners, revenue reporting and unit economics

 - Find fraudulent and abusive patterns across onboarding, funding, card spend and transfers, and build the signals and rules that let risk and operations act on them

 - Treat data quality, testing, access control and PII handling as part of the platform, not an afterthought

 - Choose tools deliberately, set standards for the function and hire the team as Plasma scales

The Bar

 - A senior, hands-on data practitioner with a track record of both building a data platform and using it

 - Deep SQL and data modelling skills, with enough engineering range to build and run production pipelines yourself

 - Comfortable starting from very little, and building something that still makes sense when the team is five times bigger

 - Strong judgment on tradeoffs: speed vs. rigour, build vs. buy, a quick answer now vs. a reusable model later

 - You turn analysis into decisions. You can explain a finding to a non-technical leader in a few sentences and tell them what to do about it

 - You communicate clearly, write clean, tested code, and lead through technical decisions whether or not you're managing people yet

 - You have very high agency. You don't wait to be told which problem to work on; you go and find the ones that matter



Nice to have

 - You've been an early or founding data hire at a fast-growing fintech

 - Experience with real money data at a fintech: payments, cards, ledgers, settlement, chargebacks or FX. You know the ways financial data goes wrong

 - Hands-on fraud, risk or financial-crime analytics

 - Familiarity with stablecoins and on-chain data, including how blockchain transactions map to accounts, balances and ledgers

 - Experience hiring and growing a data team

 - Machine learning in production for fraud, risk or personalisation


WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU

 - Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.

 - A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.

 - Premium health insurance for you and your family, fully covered by Plasma.

 - Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.

 - All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.

 - Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.



Data Protection & Privacy
We are committed to protecting the privacy and security of your personal data. Any personal information you provide during the recruitment process will be processed in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable local data protection laws.

title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Evaluation Infrastructure
description:
About Turing
Turing’s mission is to accelerate superintelligence to drive real economic progress. Headquartered in San Francisco, Turing works with frontier AI labs to generate high-quality datasets, reinforcement learning environments, and frontier research benchmarks that improve model capabilities in software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and advanced STEM reasoning. In software engineering, Turing is the largest and longest-running data provider in the category. Turing also works with Fortune 500 enterprises across financial services, life sciences, healthcare, retail, automotive, and CPG to build and deploy end-to-end agentic AI systems inside mission-critical workflows. By operating on both sides, Turing closes the loop between frontier research and enterprise deployment, turning real-world deployment signals into better data, evaluations, and more capable models. Learn more at www.turing.com .
Senior Software Engineer, AI Evaluation Infrastructure
We build the infrastructure that frontier AI labs use to evaluate coding agents and language models: benchmark datasets, agent evaluation runs at scale, and automated task quality checks. You would own features across the stack, from the data model and background jobs to the screens our users work in every day.
This is a role for an experienced engineer who works independently, makes sound tradeoffs, and turns a loosely defined request into something shipped, tested, and safe to leave alone.
What you will do
• Design and ship features end to end: data model, API, background workers, and the UI when the change needs it.
• Build and improve how agents and models are evaluated: running trials in sandboxed environments, scoring results, and turning thousands of runs into results people can trust.
• Improve how benchmark tasks are quality-checked: verifiers, rubric-based and LLM-as-a-judge grading, and deciding whether a task is clear, solvable, and fair to score.
• Integrate new models, agents, and benchmarks in a way that generalizes, without a special case for each one.
• Keep the system fast and reliable as usage grows: efficient queries, safe migrations, and concurrency that holds up under load.
• Review teammates’ pull requests against our engineering guidelines and help keep the codebase consistent.
What you bring
• 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with ownership of at least one service from design through on-call.
• Bachelor’s degree or higher in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
• Strong Python and experience with Django (or a similar framework), PostgreSQL, and a task queue such as Celery. What matters most is having run a real system, not knowing a particular framework.
• Hands-on experience in LLM evaluation, beyond calling a model API. You understand how a benchmark task is built, how an agent trial is scored, and how results are aggregated and compared. Experience with Harbor, Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench, Inspect, or a similar harness is a strong plus.
• Judgment about task quality. You can spot ambiguous instructions, weak or gameable verifiers, leaked answers, and checks that pass for the wrong reason.
• Good tradeoffs. You reach for the smallest design that solves the problem, extend what already exists before adding something new, and can explain what you chose not to build.
• Ownership. You take a fuzzy request, find the relevant code, ask questions only when the answer changes the design, and finish the job, including migrations, tests, and edge cases users will hit.
• Quick adoption of team conventions. You read the written guidelines and your first pull requests already match them in naming, structure, tests, and error handling.
• Comfort with a TypeScript and React frontend when a change is visible there. You don’t need to be a frontend specialist.
• Clear writing. Your pull request descriptions and design notes explain why, not just what.
Nice to have
• Experience running agents in sandboxed or containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes, or cloud sandboxes such as Modal or Daytona).
• Experience with LLM-as-a-judge or rubric-based grading, and with reducing judge bias and noise.
• Familiarity with coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, or OpenHands, and with MCP.
• Experience with distributed job scheduling, concurrency limits, or database locking at scale.
• Contributions to open-source evaluation or infrastructure projects.
How we work
• Written engineering guidelines, applied consistently, with the same review bar for everyone.
• Business logic lives in services. Hot paths stay cheap. Lint and tests pass before a pull request is ready.
• The same vocabulary in the code, the API, and the UI.
• We prefer deleting code to adding it, and simple designs to clever ones.
A strong first month looks like several changes merged with light review, and one area of the system you can change confidently without a guide.
Compensation: $170,000 - $200,000 Base Salary + Equity

• We are client first: We put our clients at the center of everything we do, because their success is the ultimate measure of our value.
• We work at Start-Up Speed: We move fast, stay agile and favor action because momentum is the foundation of perfection
• We are AI forward: We help our clients build the future of Al and implement it in our own roles and workflow to amplify productivity.
Advantages of joining Turing
• Work at the frontier of AI , helping the world’s leading AI labs improve their most advanced models by building expert datasets, RL environments, and first-of-a-kind benchmarks.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

We're hiring a Senior or Staff Liaison Engineer to be the engineering point of contact for hardware issues affecting V-BAT production, testing and fielded aircraft. This person holds engineering authority for nonconformance (NCR) and Material Review Board (MRB) dispositions, which covers anything that isn't simply reworked to print, including use-as-is and repair. They pull in Structures, Thermal and Design when they need specialist input to confirm a path forward. 

The ideal candidate is the person Production and Quality go to when they ask, "I have this problem, how do I solve it?" They own the answer from start to finish: the disposition, the rework or repair instructions, the drawing updates, and the long-term corrective action that keeps the problem from coming back. Composite repair experience is essential. This role is focused on liaison and sustaining engineering, not new-product design. 

What you'll do:

 - 

 - Lead the resolution of mechanical issues arising from production, testing, fielded aircraft and customer operations, including hands-on support during builds, integration and troubleshooting.

 - Serve as the engineering point of contact and approval authority for NCR and MRB dispositions, bringing in Structures, Thermal and Design as needed to confirm a path forward.

 - Disposition nonconformances as use-as-is, repair, rework, scrap or return to vendor, with documented reasoning about the effect on form, fit, function and structural integrity.

 - Evaluate and disposition issues across a wide range of hardware, including metallic, composite and plastic parts, wire harnesses and electronic assemblies.

 - Write rework and repair instructions for individual NCRs and for standard pre-approved repairs, including inspection and acceptance criteria.

 - Partner with Quality to drive issues to resolution and lead formal root cause and corrective action (RCCA) investigations when needed, using fault trees, 5 Whys, failure analysis and test-based troubleshooting.

 - Coordinate investigations across Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Test and Field Operations.

 - Decide when issues need changes to designs, drawings, processes, inspections or supplier controls, and drive CAD, drawing, specification and BOM updates through release.

 - Track recurring nonconformances and feed lessons learned back into designs and processes. 

Required qualifications:

 - 

 - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering or a related field.

 - 5+ years of relevant experience for Senior Engineer, or 8+ years for Staff Engineer

 - Experience reviewing and dispositioning NCRs within an MRB process in aerospace, defense or another regulated industry.

 - Experience supporting production, sustaining engineering, fielded products or complex hardware troubleshooting.

 - Experience writing rework or repair instructions for production hardware.

 - A track record of resolving technical issues through verified corrective action, including formal RCCA.

 - Proficiency with 3D CAD, engineering drawings, GD&T and mechanical design for manufacturing.

 - Strong technical writing and documentation skills, and clear communication across teams. 

Preferred Qualifications

 - 

 - Experience as a liaison or MRB engineer on aircraft or UAS production.

 - Experience classifying structural versus non-structural repairs, or writing standard repair procedures or structural repair manuals.

 - Working knowledge of composite materials, processes and inspection methods, such as prepreg, wet layup, bonding, cure cycles, tap testing and ultrasonic testing.

 - Familiarity with workmanship standards for wire harnesses and electronic assemblies, such as IPC/WHMA-A-620 and IPC-A-610.

 - Familiarity with metallic and plastic manufacturing processes, finishes and common defect modes.

 - Ability to assess structural margin, or experience working closely with stress and thermal analysts.

 - Experience in an AS9100 quality environment.

 - Experience with Siemens NX and Teamcenter.

 - Experience supporting fielded aircraft and customer operations.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


Key Overview:
As a Member of Technical Staff in Post-Training, you will train our large language models (LLMs) with reinforcement learning and develop methods that help them generalize beyond the distribution they were trained on. You will design the training recipes, environments, and evaluations that tell us whether a model has truly learned a skill or has only fitted its training tasks, and turn what works into the recipes behind our production models. You will work closely with the post-training data infrastructure, evaluation, and pre-training teams.

Key Responsibilities

 - Design, run, and analyse large-scale RL post-training experiments (e.g., RLHF, RL from verifiable rewards).

 - Research and develop methods that improve out-of-distribution generalization, such as reward design, environment and task diversity, curricula, and regularization.

 - Build held-out evaluations that measure generalization to unseen tasks, domains, and formats, and that catch reward hacking and benchmark overfitting.

 - Diagnose training dynamics and failure modes, including instability, reward over-optimization, and capability regressions.

 - Turn successful research into robust, reproducible training recipes for production models.


Qualifications

 - Strong research and software engineering skills, with hands-on experience training LLMs.

 - Experience applying reinforcement learning to LLMs (e.g., PPO, GRPO, RLHF, RLVR), ideally at scale.

 - Track record of work on generalization, robustness, or distribution shift, through publications or shipped models.

 - Rigorous experimental practice: clean ablations, careful controls, and sound conclusions from noisy results.

 - Experience with distributed training (e.g., JAX, PyTorch, FSDP, Megatron) is a plus.

 - Excellent communication skills.

 - Deep understanding of data quality principles and best practices: demonstrates willingness to dive deep into data while possessing strong intuition for assessing the quality of datasets and anticipating how different data characteristics will impact model training outcomes.
   

Working Location
This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.

 




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.

description:
About Tinybird
At Tinybird, we help developers and data teams take flight by unlocking the power of real-time data to build data products faster. With Tinybird, developers can easily ingest data from multiple sources, query it using the SQL they already know and love, and publish results as low-latency, high-concurrency APIs for their applications — all in minutes, not hours or days.

Our mission is to make real-time data accessible and actionable for every developer. Tinybird is loved by developers and trusted by data engineers at some of the world’s leading companies. We’re growing quickly and expanding our marketing team to amplify our reach and accelerate our demand engine.

About the Role
We're hiring a EU based growth lead to help drive expansion of our product suite. Thousands of developers try our products every quarter. Your job is to create much more of that demand, and to make sure the right people become real conversations with our sales team. This is a builder role, not a channel-management or pure strategy role. You'll work directly with our CEO, engineering, design, content, RevOps and sales.
What you'll do
•
Run the funnel. You own signups, activation, and qualified pipeline from developer-led sources. You'll build one weekly view from signup to activation to opportunity, report it, and act on it.
•
Make sure no hot lead goes cold. You'll define what "high intent" means with RevOps and sales, and build the scoring, routing and alerts so those leads get a human touch within one business day.
•
Ship something public every week. You'll partner with engineers and our content team on demos, examples, teardowns and build-in-public posts that ride what developers are talking about right now. You set the calendar and priorities, and you build and write a meaningful share yourself.
•
Get Tinybird into AI-native workflows. This is a new challenge for us and requires experimentation and the right ability to test and iterate. It means agent skills, MCP servers, plugins for Cursor, Claude and OpenAI, and showing up well in AI assistants' answers. You'll test, measure what drives signups, and double down or drop it quickly.
•
Run focused campaigns, one at a time. Each has a target list, an offer, and a sales follow-up.
•
Improve activation. You'll own the lifecycle emails and in-product nudges in HubSpot, with the goal of getting people to a first query, not just an open.
•
Reallocate fast. You'll shift time and budget toward what produces pipeline, reviewing monthly and adjusting within weeks.
Your first 90 days
•
A single, trusted signup-to-pipeline dashboard, reviewed weekly with sales and the CEO.
•
Routing and first-touch SLAs live, with the first-touch rate measured.
•
A weekly public shipping cadence running, and at least one targeted campaign launched with sales follow-up.
What you bring
•
You've owned a signup-to-pipeline or signup-to-revenue number at a developer-facing product (devtools, data, infrastructure, observability, security or similar), and you can tell us specifically what you changed and what happened.
•
You're technical enough to build. You write SQL, spin up a working demo, read an API reference, and use AI coding tools daily. Engineers take your work seriously because you ship it.
•
You've marketed to technical buyers, from individual developers up to platform and data leads.
•
You move fast and learn in public. Show us something you shipped in the last 90 days: an experiment, a demo, a campaign, a side project.
•
About 5+ years in growth, demand gen or developer marketing, with enough experience to work independently and enough appetite to still do the work yourself.
Nice to have
•
Experience with ClickHouse, Kafka, or analytics and real-time data infrastructure
•
Hands-on HubSpot, or comparable CRM and attribution tooling
•
A network among AI-native builders, or experience growing a developer community
•
Experience with a PLG-to-enterprise transition
Why You’ll Love Working at Tinybird
•
You’ll join a fast-growing, transparent, and collaborative company where your work has real impact.
We’re remote-first, but you’ll have opportunities to connect with your teammates at company offsites and events.
•
Learning and growth are part of our DNA — we encourage curiosity and initiative.
•
Diversity and inclusion are central to our values. We welcome all applicants, even if you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications.
•
Real technical problem, real customers, real traction — this is not a pre-product-market-fit role
•
You'll own the function from day one with huge opportunity to make an impact for the business and direct access to the founding team
•
The product is genuinely differentiated in a market that is growing fast
How We Work
•
This is a fully remote role. If you’re based in Madrid or nearby, we’d love to see you at the office, where the team regularly gets together to work and spend time together.
•
As we’re in the early stages, your contributions will have a significant impact on everything we do.
•
We believe in transparency, so you’ll always be in the loop about what’s happening.
Check out our blog or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s important to us.

You'll help define and drive that broader vision across teams, proposing ambitious research directions and taking direct ownership of the design and implementation of its most critical components. You'll work directly with our voice lead and collaborate tightly with our video teams and other senior members of the org.

Concretely, you'll work on voice to voice models that produce text and voice simultaneously. Models that can reason, interrupt the user with back channeling and talk. Models that feel like you are having a natural conversation with, without the feeling of turn taking that is dominant in current speech to speech models. Your role would be to partner in defining a roadmap, implementing it and shipping the outcomes to product.

What you'll do


 - Shape our roadmap to create new model capabilities and unlock new functionality for our customer base, on both short and long time horizons.

 - Develop and evaluate streaming and conversational systems for low-latency, interactive voice-video synthesis.

 - Implement and bring designs to life, from pretraining through post-training.

 - Integrate and test novel architectures (neural codecs, diffusion, flow-matching) to enhance realism and responsiveness.

 - Define new evaluation metrics for conversational systems, including latency-aware and interaction-based measurements.
